setup_summary.text: Q3 2026 (reported 23 Oct; 10-Q filed 28 Oct): revenue was $9.45B, +5.8% YoY and about +5% sequentially, led by a 13% sequential rise in the Middle East. GAAP diluted EPS was $0.49 against $0.50 a year ago.

Adjusted EPS excluding charges was $0.64, up $0.09 sequentially and down $0.05 YoY. The gap to GAAP is a $0.12 ($187M) non-cash pension settlement charge and $0.03 of ChampionX merger and integration costs. Pre-print consensus was $0.62 EPS on $9.27B revenue, so the quarter beat on both.

Nine-month revenue is +4.5% but net income is -10.9% and diluted EPS -16.1%. Excluding ChampionX, revenue is down 4%, driven by a 16% (~$1.1B) Middle East decline from conflict disruptions. Margins are the weak point.

Q4 FY2026 will be reported on 2027-01-21 after the close (Finnhub). Consensus is EPS $0.75 and revenue $10.01B. Management guided Q4 revenue to ~$10B (+5-7% sequential) and adjusted EBITDA margin up 100-150 bps from 21.9%, so consensus sits at the middle of guidance.

The consensus-implied +36.3% EPS growth compares $0.75 with a GAAP Q4 2025 EPS of $0.55 that carried $561M of pretax charges. The comparison is not like-for-like. The consensus revenue growth of +2.7% YoY is a cleaner comparison.

The average closing move over the last 8 reports is ±4.1%. No options-implied move is available yet. The stock closed at $53.74 on 30 Oct. The CEO (10b5-1 plan), the CAO and the CLO sold shares in the days after the print. Plan-based sales are routine, so this is a weak signal.
Net debt was $9.25B at 30 Sep, up $1.8B YTD. The pending Kelvion deal (~$3.4B cash plus ~$0.7B assumed debt, closing 1H27) adds roughly $4B on a simple sum, putting pro forma net debt above $13B.

consensus.text: Consensus revenue is $10.01B, +2.7% YoY and about +5.9% sequential.

view.text: Guidance of ~$10B (+5-7% sequential) implies $9.92-10.11B, so consensus is mid-range. The guide assumes Middle East revenue flat at ~$1.9B. Upside needs the Middle East or year-end Digital and product sales to beat. Downside is a worsening of the late-Q3 disruptions.

consensus.text: Consensus EPS is $0.75, +$0.11 sequentially. Whether it is on an adjusted basis is not stated in the sources.

view.text: My rough bridge: ~$0.22B of incremental EBITDA from the guide, taxed at ~21% over ~1.5B diluted shares, adds about $0.11-0.13. That gives roughly $0.75-0.77, in line with consensus. The bar is therefore the top of guidance, not a soft number. This is my arithmetic, not company guidance.

last_reported.text: Q3 adjusted EBITDA margin was 21.9%, up 71 bps sequentially.

view.text: Guidance is +100-150 bps, to about 22.9-23.4%. Drivers are Middle East operating leverage on retained resources and year-end Digital exploration and product sales. Offsets are Data Center Solutions ramp costs and mix, which the CFO called non-accretive, plus pricing pressure.

last_reported.text: Q3 Middle East revenue was $1.9B, +13% sequentially despite late-quarter disruptions.

view.text: Guidance assumes flat at ~$1.9B, which is ~83% of Q4 2025 (implying ~$2.3B then). This is the main swing factor for revenue and margin. Management said the late-Q3 activity adjustments were stabilizing, and the Saudi integrated well construction contracts mobilize in Q4 and reach full capacity in 2027.

last_reported.text: Q3 Production Systems revenue was $4.0B (+6% sequentially) at a 16.1% pretax margin.

view.text: Guidance is high-single-digit sequential growth, about $4.3-4.4B on my math, helped by year-end product sales, OneSubsea and ChampionX. Well Construction and Reservoir Performance are guided essentially flat. Watch Production Systems for the combined core growth of low single digits.

last_reported.text: Q3 Digital revenue was $693M (-1% sequential) at a 28% pretax margin. Nine-month revenue was $2.03B, +11%.

view.text: Management guides Q4 up in line with history on a 'significant' uptick in exploration data sales, with full-year growth in the double digits and adjusted EBITDA margin above 35%. Against FY2025 Digital of $2.66B, +10% implies Q4 of at least ~$0.9B, versus $825M in Q4 2025. My arithmetic.

last_reported.text: Q3 free cash flow was $828M, and 9M FCF was $1.52B against $1.83B a year earlier. The XBRL-derived figure of $2.07B subtracts capex only, so the definitions differ. Q4 2025 FCF on the company definition was ~$2.29B (FY $4.115B less 9M $1.826B).

view.text: Management expects a 'meaningful step-up' from lower inventory and higher collections, but the size depends on the timing of collections in certain countries. Receivables rose ~$1.05B YTD and the 9M working-capital outflow was $1.55B. A Q4 near last year's ~$2.3B would be a solid result, and anything well below it points to a collections slip.

last_reported.text: 9M capital investments were $1.8B. Q3 buybacks were $656M (12.9M shares at $51.01) and 9M buybacks were $1.755B.

view.text: The FY guides of ~$2.5B capex and ~$2.4B buybacks imply Q4 of about $0.65-0.7B for each. Total 2026 shareholder returns will be slightly above $4B. Watch whether Kelvion funding changes the buyback pace in 2027.

last_reported.text: The Q3 rate was 23% (non-deductible $187M pension charge) against 20% in Q2 and 21% for 9M.

view.text: The rate should return toward ~20-21% with no pension charge. No explicit Q4 guide is given.

since_filing.text: The 10-Q matches the earlier results release and call: revenue $9.449B, GAAP EPS $0.49 and the $187M pension charge. The call's adjusted EPS of $0.64 reconciles to GAAP by adding back $0.12 (pension) and $0.03 (merger and integration). No contradictions were found. The call transcript is undated, and M.04 and N.05 place the results on 23 Oct.

Insider activity after the 10-Q: the CEO sold 25,000 shares at $53.17 on 27 Oct under a 10b5-1 plan adopted 27 May. The CAO sold 10,047 shares (~$539K) on 29 Oct and the CLO sold ~$1.12M (reported 31 Oct). The stock closed at $53.74 on 30 Oct. Vanguard reported a 4.97% passive stake.

The date of the next report is inconsistent across sources. Finnhub shows 2027-01-21 after the close (fiscal Q4), while an Investing.com page dated 25 Oct shows 14 Jan 2027. Both are third-party data and the date is not confirmed by the company. The CFO referenced 'January' for 2027 color.

The 10-Q reports no material changes to risk factors since the 10-K. New developments versus the 10-K are the Middle East conflict disruptions to 2026 results, the Kelvion agreement signed 31 Aug 2026, the $2.0B of debt issued in Q2 2026 and the Q3 pension settlement.

key_debates.question: Can Q4 deliver ~$10B and +100-150 bps of EBITDA margin with the Middle East flat?

bull.text: Q4 is seasonally strong: year-end Digital exploration, product and OneSubsea sales. In Q4 2025, organic revenue rose sequentially in both North America (+6%) and international (+7%). ChampionX is at record revenue and margin, and the Saudi contracts mobilize in Q4. Management has built operating leverage by retaining Middle East resources.

bear.text: Consensus ($10.01B revenue, $0.75 EPS) already sits on the guide, leaving little cushion. The guide depends on Middle East stability after late-Q3 disruptions and 'heightened tensions', and Iraq did not recover in Q3. Digital exploration sales are lumpy: Q3 fell $48M after a strong Q2.

key_debates.what_settles_it: The 21 Jan print: Middle East revenue against $1.9B, Digital exploration sales, Production Systems growth versus the high-single-digit guide and adjusted EBITDA margin against 22.9-23.4%.

key_debates.question: Will Middle East recovery lift margins, or do pricing, inflation and Data Center mix cap them?

bull.text: Middle East dilution was the main driver of 2026 margin compression, with 9M Reservoir Performance and Well Construction margins down 212 bps and 346 bps. Operating leverage should return as activity rebounds. Inflation is largely baked in, ChampionX synergies exceed plan, and Digital margins are above 35% EBITDA.

bear.text: Well Construction margin pressure was 'compounded by pricing headwinds in select markets', and management said larger Middle East tenders carry pricing pressure. Data Center Solutions is not accretive to company margin and carries ramp costs. Full 2027 margin guidance is deferred to January.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Division margins in Q4 (Well Construction 16.4% and Reservoir Performance 16.3% in Q3 versus 19% and 20% in Q4 2025) and the 2027 margin framework in January.

key_debates.question: Is cash conversion recovering, and is the balance sheet ready for Kelvion plus buybacks?

bull.text: Q4 is historically the cash-heavy quarter: FY2025 FCF was $4.1B, with ~$2.3B in Q4. Management expects a meaningful step-up and has $5.0B of undrawn facilities and $3.6B of cash and short-term investments. Total returns of slightly above $4B are maintained.

bear.text: 9M FCF is $1.52B against $1.83B, and net debt rose $1.8B YTD to $9.25B. Receivables are up ~$1.05B and working capital absorbed $1.55B. Kelvion adds ~$4B of cash plus debt in 1H27 while buybacks continue.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 FCF against the ~$2.3B prior-year level, year-end net debt, DSO and any update on Kelvion financing or buyback pacing.

key_debates.question: Is the 2027 upcycle durable enough to support outperformance even without a Middle East fix?

bull.text: Management cites third-party deepwater FIDs +30% in 2026, a rebound in exploration, the Venezuela activation (revenue to more than double this year, multifold in 2027), Saudi multi-year well construction awards, backlog up to $6.8B and OneSubsea bookings above $9B. It sees core divisions outperforming mid-single-digit market growth.

bear.text: The 2027 market outlook assumes the Middle East stays at 2H26 levels and no escalation. An analyst question raised a Middle East resolution pushing crude back to $65-70 as a risk to growth drivers. Management declined to give regional 2027 detail, and the 2027 view is not yet supported by reported numbers.

key_debates.what_settles_it: The January 2027 outlook, including 2027 margin color, plus OneSubsea bookings, Venezuela revenue, and customer budget announcements.

scenarios.name: base

description.text: Q4 revenue lands near ~$10.0B (+5-7% sequential) and adjusted EPS near $0.75-0.77. Middle East revenue is flat at ~$1.9B, margin expands about 125 bps and FCF steps up. Management frames 2027 as mid-single-digit market growth with outperformance. The stock reaction stays within the ±4% average range.

triggers: Production Systems up high single digits

description.text: Revenue reaches the high end or above (>$10.1B), Middle East recovery resumes ahead of the flat assumption, Digital exploration and OneSubsea beat, and EBITDA margin expands at or above 150 bps. EPS is $0.80 or better, and the 2027 guide leans toward 'visible outperformance' on larger bookings and Venezuela.

scenarios.name: bear

description.text: Middle East disruption escalates or persists below $1.9B, Q4 revenue falls short of $9.9B, Digital exploration disappoints and Data Center ramp costs and pricing pressure cap margin expansion. FCF falls short of the usual Q4 step-up because of collections timing, and 2027 guidance is hedged on Middle East uncertainty.

triggers: Weaker tone on 2027 Middle East or pricing

claim.text: Middle East conflict: revenue there was down 16% over 9M. The Q4 guide assumes stability, and management cites 'heightened tensions' and late-Q3 disruptions. Escalation breaks the guide and the 2027 market assumption.

Collections and working capital: receivables rose to $9.7B from $8.7B at year-end, and the Q4 FCF step-up depends on the timing of collections in certain countries. Revenue in excess of billings on over-time contracts rose to $0.6B from $0.4B.

Margin dilution and pricing: Data Center Solutions ramp costs reduced All Other operating income despite revenue growth. The CFO says it is not accretive to company margin. Pricing headwinds in Well Construction and larger Middle East tenders persist.
Kelvion acquisition: ~$3.4B cash plus ~$0.7B assumed debt, subject to regulatory approvals, closing in 1H27. It adds leverage, integration and execution risk, and competes with buybacks for cash.
Ongoing integration of ChampionX: synergies are ahead of plan, but the 10-K flags the risk that benefits are not fully realized, and chemical inflation is partly offsetting margins.

Oil price and customer spending risk: an easing in crude (the analyst's $65-70 scenario) could soften activity, and 82% of 2025 revenue is outside the US. The 10-K cites commodity-price, geopolitical, sanctions (including Russia, ~4% of revenue) and FX exposures.

questions_for_management.question: What does the flat ~$1.9B Middle East Q4 assumption embed by country, and what exit rate did Q3 end at after the late-quarter disruptions?

why.text: The Q3 beat was ahead of expectations before disruptions hit, and the guide hinges on this assumption.

questions_for_management.question: How much Q4 free cash flow do you expect, and which countries or customers drive collection timing?

why.text: 9M FCF is down YoY, receivables are up ~$1.05B and the step-up is 'dependent on timing in certain countries'.

questions_for_management.question: How do you expect 2027 margins to evolve, given retained Middle East capacity, Data Center mix dilution and pricing pressure?

why.text: The CFO deferred the 2027 margin equation to January, and margins are the main driver of the 9M EPS decline.

questions_for_management.question: How will Kelvion be financed, and does it change the 2027 buyback pace and leverage targets?

why.text: The deal adds ~$4B of cash and debt, while net debt is already up $1.8B YTD and buybacks run at ~$2.4B a year.

questions_for_management.question: What is the size and timing of the Q4 Digital exploration uplift, and what does it imply for FY Digital growth and the >35% margin?

why.text: Q3 exploration sales fell $48M sequentially after a strong Q2, and the FY target requires a large Q4.

questions_for_management.question: What is your Venezuela revenue and credit exposure, and how do you manage payment risk as activity scales toward multifold growth?

why.text: Management called Venezuela a major 2027 driver with a potential ~$1B long-term revenue ambition.
